device.name: OmniIsaacGymEnvs Cartpole (Isaac Sim 4.0 vectorised RL environment)

facts.text: The repository contains reinforcement-learning examples that run with Isaac Sim and are built on omni.isaac.core and omni.isaac.gym
The examples rely on the latest Isaac Sim release and pin it to 4.0.0, installed separately
VecEnvRLGames extends VecEnvBase, imported from omni.isaac.gym.vec_env, so its simulator and base interface come from outside the clone
VecEnvRLGames.step takes an actions tensor and returns four values: an observation dict, rewards, resets and extras
VecEnvRLGames.reset takes seed and options, resets the task, applies one zero action and returns the observation dict; its body does not read seed or options
The observation dict carries the observations under obs and the task states under states
The observations are clamped to +-clipObservations in the wrapper
The actions are clamped to +-clipActions before the task sees them
Cartpole sets clipActions to 1.0, clipObservations to 5.0, resetDist to 3.0 and maxEffort to 400.0
RLTask initializes a task's action space to a Box of -1 to 1 per action dimension and its observation space to a Box of -inf to inf per observation dimension unless the task sets its own
CartpoleTask declares four observations and one action
The Cartpole observation is [cart position, cart velocity, pole position, pole velocity]
The Cartpole action is a force on the cart: maxEffort times the first action component
A Cartpole reset samples the cart position in [-1, 1], the pole position in [-0.125 pi, 0.125 pi], the cart velocity in [-0.5, 0.5] and the pole velocity in [-0.25 pi, 0.25 pi]
The Cartpole reward is 1 - pole_pos^2 - 0.01*|cart_vel| - 0.005*|pole_vel|, replaced by -2 when |cart_pos| > resetDist or |pole_pos| > pi/2
Cartpole flags a reset when |cart_pos| > resetDist, |pole_pos| > pi/2, or the progress reaches the episode length
The Cartpole episode length is 500 steps
Cartpole sets controlFrequencyInv to 2 (about 60 Hz) and the physics dt to 0.0083 s (1/120 s)
Cartpole defaults to 512 environments
The Hydra task map maps the name Cartpole to CartpoleTask
initialize_task instantiates task_map[cfg['task_name']]
The training script constructs VecEnvRLGames with headless, sim_device, livestream, viewport and experience arguments
The install_requires list is numpy, protobuf, omegaconf, hydra-core, urllib3, rl-games, moviepy and gymnasium 0.28.1

determinism.notes: the fake reseeds Python's random.Random from reset(seed) or cap.world.seed.v1 and its step is deterministic, so one seed repeats a trajectory; the upstream reset accepts but ignores seed (vec_env_rlgames.py:106-115) and draws resets with torch's generator, so a seed does not repeat an upstream run

gaps: analytic stand-in with no rigid-body dynamics, contacts, friction, actuator, sensor or noise model: the action sets two placeholder velocities, so this is F0 and its trajectories are not Isaac Sim's
Isaac Sim 4.0.0 and PhysX are external (README.md:31-33) and were never opened here; no sim backend is offered, only the package fake

the upstream is vectorised over num_envs (512 by default, Cartpole.yaml:8) and returns per-environment reward and reset tensors plus an obs/states dict (vec_env_rlgames.py:102-104); this package serves one environment, so reward and done are scalars and the observation is a four-vector

reset differs: VecEnvRLGames applies one zero action after task.reset and ignores seed/options (vec_env_rlgames.py:106-115); the fake seeds its own random generator and returns the initial state without that extra step
no rendering, viewport recording, cameras, domain randomisation or task states are modelled; snapshots are not offered because the environment exposes no get_state/set_state
the fake was never compared with an Isaac Sim run and no hardware or real-simulator evidence exists

measures.description: Last observation (derived from the observation space)
measures.name: observation

safe_state.description: the fake stops advancing: the runtime's e-stop latch refuses every step, reset and seed until mhs.safety.reset, and the last observation, tick and episode stay readable
